es: Reconocer en una propuesta de barrio sus cuatro partes (objetivo, beneficio, plan y petición) y los verbos que sugieren y justifican.

teaching.en: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.
teaching.es: El objetivo de esta propuesta es convertir la plaza vacía en un mercado de fin de semana donde los productores locales puedan alquilar un puesto, y se ha consultado a todas las partes interesadas.
teaching.explanationEs: The objective is to… abre la propuesta y dice qué se quiere lograr.
segments: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend
market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.
teaching.audioText: The objective of this proposal is to turn the empty square into a weekend market where local growers can rent a stall, and every stakeholder has been consulted.

teaching.en: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.
teaching.es: El beneficio más tangible es que las familias por fin tendrán un lugar seguro donde reunirse, algo que al barrio le ha faltado durante años.
teaching.explanationEs: Tangible benefit: una ventaja concreta que se puede ver o medir, no una promesa vaga.
segments: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a
safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.
teaching.audioText: The most tangible benefit is that families will finally have a safe place to meet, something the neighbourhood has lacked for years.

teaching.en: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty stalls in May and opening to the public in June.
teaching.es: Esbozamos tres etapas: limpiar la plaza en abril, montar veinte puestos en mayo y abrir al público en junio.
teaching.explanationEs: We outline… presenta el plan a grandes rasgos, en pasos ordenados.
segments: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty
stalls in May and opening to the public in June.
teaching.audioText: We outline three stages: clearing the square in April, building twenty stalls in May and opening to the public in June.

teaching.en: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.
teaching.es: Tras sopesar los costes, recomendamos celebrar el mercado los sábados, porque es cuando casi todos los vecinos están libres, lo que da a la propuesta un argumento convincente.
teaching.explanationEs: We recommend + -ing: el autor aconseja y justifica en la misma frase.
segments: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that
is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.
teaching.audioText: After weighing the costs, we recommend holding the market on Saturdays, because that is when most residents are free, which gives the proposal a compelling argument.

teaching.en: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council, which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.
teaching.es: Solicitamos respetuosamente una subvención de 4.000 dólares al consejo, que cubriría el coste de los puestos y del seguro.
teaching.explanationEs: We request… formula la petición, casi siempre al final y con tono cortés.
segments: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council,
which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.
teaching.audioText: We respectfully request a grant of 4,000 dollars from the council, which would cover the cost of the stalls and the insurance.

teaching.en: Tonight Ana will give a short pitch to put forward the idea, and two shop owners will endorse it, but the written proposal has every detail.
teaching.es: Esta noche Ana hará una presentación breve para plantear la idea y dos comerciantes la respaldarán, pero la propuesta escrita tiene todos los detalles.
teaching.explanationEs: Pitch es la versión oral y corta; put forward = plantear una idea; endorse = respaldarla públicamente.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte de una propuesta es este párrafo del borrador?

choices.text: It states the objective of the project.
It lists the benefits for local residents.
It makes a formal request for money.

feedback.es: El párrafo dice qué se quiere lograr («Our aim is to convert…»): es el objetivo, no la lista de beneficios ni una petición.

hint.es: Busca qué quiere conseguir el proyecto; no hay cifras ni dinero solicitado.

origin.text: Young people in the neighbourhood have nowhere to meet after school, and the bus service stops at six. Our aim is to turn the old depot into a workshop where teenagers can learn practical skills.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo es dar a los jóvenes un sitio donde aprender oficios.»

feedback.es: The objective is to + verbo base nombra lo que la propuesta quiere lograr.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que abre la propuesta y nombra lo que se quiere lograr.

origin.text: The proposal is to turn the old depot into a youth workshop. The ___ is to give teenagers somewhere to learn practical skills after school.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esta noche Ana planteará nuestra propuesta ante el consejo.»

answer.text: Tonight Ana will put forward our proposal to the council

feedback.es: Put forward + la idea o la propuesta significa plantearla ante un órgano o un público.

hint.es: Empieza por el adverbio de tiempo y deja al consejo para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué petición hace el equipo al final.

choices.text: Permission to use the library building on Saturdays.
Money from the council to help pay for the market.
Twenty volunteers to build the stalls in May.

feedback.es: La petición llega en la última frase: «we request a grant… from the council»; la biblioteca solo da nombre al lugar y los voluntarios no se mencionan.

origin.audio: Good evening, everyone. Our objective is to turn the empty car park behind the library into a weekend market with twenty stalls. The main benefit is tangible: local growers will earn a fair income, and families will have somewhere safe to meet. We outline three stages: clearing the site in April, building the stalls in May and opening in June. We recommend holding the market on Saturdays, when most residents are free. Finally, we request a grant of four thousand dollars from the council.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una propuesta con la parte que cumple.

pairs: The objective is to reduce litter on the riverside path.
The most tangible benefit is that children will walk to school safely.
We outline two stages: clearing in spring and planting in autumn.
We respectfully request a grant of 2,000 dollars.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula delata su parte: objective (qué), benefit (para quién), outline (cómo) y request (qué se pide).

pairs: The objective is to reduce litter on the riverside path.
The most tangible benefit is that children will walk to school safely.
We outline two stages: clearing in spring and planting in autumn.
We respectfully request a grant of 2,000 dollars.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso. ¿Qué diferencia se da a entender entre el pitch y la propuesta escrita?

choices.text: The pitch replaces the document, so nobody needs to read it.
The document summarises what Ana will say on Thursday.
The pitch only introduces the idea; the document holds the detail.

feedback.es: El pitch es breve y sirve para plantear la idea; los datos completos (presupuesto y calendario) están en el documento escrito.

origin.text: Notice: On Thursday Ana will put forward the idea in a five-minute pitch. The full proposal, with the budget and the calendar, will be available on paper at the library from Friday.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué finalidad escribe Mia este correo?

choices.text: To ask for funding and support for a book swap.
To announce that the book swap has been approved.
To complain that the library is used too little.

feedback.es: Mia plantea una propuesta y pide una subvención: busca apoyo y dinero, no anuncia una aprobación ni se queja.

origin.text: Dear Ms Okafor, I am writing to put forward a proposal for a Saturday book swap in the library garden. The main benefit is tangible: children will get free books, and the library will reach families who rarely visit it. We outline a plan in two stages, and we recommend starting in May. We request a grant of 600 dollars to cover tables and posters. Several local shops already endorse the idea.

prompt.es: Según el correo, ¿por qué menciona Mia que varios comercios respaldan la idea?

choices.text: To explain that the shops will pay for the posters.
To show that the request has support in the neighbourhood.
To warn that the plan depends on the shops opening.

feedback.es: Endorse significa respaldar: al citar a los comercios, Mia sugiere que la petición cuenta con apoyo local; no dice que paguen nada.

origin.text: Dear Ms Okafor, I am writing to put forward a proposal for a Saturday book swap in the library garden. The main benefit is tangible: children will get free books, and the library will reach families who rarely visit it. We outline a plan in two stages, and we recommend starting in May. We request a grant of 600 dollars to cover tables and posters. Several local shops already endorse the idea.

prompt.es: Completa: «El beneficio más tangible es que cuarenta familias recibirán verduras.»

feedback.es: Tangible benefit es la colocación para una ventaja concreta y medible, como las cuarenta familias.

origin.text: Every proposal needs a clear reason behind it. The most ___ benefit of the garden is that forty families will receive fresh vegetables every week.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pedimos una subvención para cubrir el coste de los puestos.»

answer.text: We request a grant to cover the cost of the stalls

feedback.es: We request + lo que pides: la subvención va justo después del verbo y el fin se añade con to cover.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué da a entender la decisión de Leo sobre el presupuesto.

choices.text: That the budget had been kept secret from the neighbours.
That the written proposal had not been sent to anyone yet.
That a pitch should persuade, while the document carries the figures.

feedback.es: Leo dejó las cifras para el documento y usó el pitch para persuadir con el beneficio: entiende cada formato con una función distinta.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting, Leo gave a five-minute pitch for a youth football league. He did not read the budget aloud. He said the written proposal, which everyone had received by email, contained every figure. Instead, he spent his time on the benefit, describing how the league would keep teenagers busy on Friday evenings.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador. ¿Qué parte de la propuesta falta todavía?

choices.text: The request for money or support.
The objective of the project.
The plan for the weekends of work.

feedback.es: El borrador tiene objetivo, beneficio, plan y recomendación, pero nadie pide nada todavía: falta la petición.

origin.text: Our objective is to paint the school gym with help from parents. The main benefit is a safer, brighter space for sport. We outline a plan with two weekends of work, and we recommend the first weekend of June.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso solicitamos una subvención de 1.500 dólares en el último párrafo.»

feedback.es: We request… es la fórmula de la petición y suele ocupar el último párrafo.

origin.text: A reader should always know what we are asking for. That is why we ___ a grant of 1,500 dollars in the final paragraph.
